item.title: Thousands will hit Houston streets for Turkey Trot races on Thanksgiving. What to know.
item.description: People run during the BakerRipley Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, Nov. 25, 2021, through the Galleria area in Houston. (Mark Mulligan/Staff photographer) Thousands of Turkey Trot runners will hit the streets across Houston Thursday morning before the Thanksgiving festivities begin. The Turkey Trot is a Thanksgiving race tradition dating back to the 1890s that has grown to become the biggest running day of the year, according to RunSignUp.com, which tracks annual stats. There are 66 scheduled events in Texas on Thanksgiving Day on FindARace.com . Houston hosts three large races. Beyond Houston, several Turkey Trots are scheduled across the surrounding area, including races in Katy, The Woodlands, Kingwood, Sugar Land, Pearland and Friendswood. Tips for running a Turkey Trot race Dr. Larry Balle, a sports medicine physician at Houston Methodist, has some tips for getting through the turkey trot, whether you're a first-timer or a regular runner. Stay hydrated, get enough sleep and avoid working out too hard the day before the race For regular runners: "You cannot make up for missed training in the final few days. If you have been running regularly, trust the work you have already put in. Keep your runs easy, stay hydrated and well-fueled, get plenty of sleep, and resist the temptation to fit in one last hard workout." For newbies: "If you're new to running, don't feel pressured to run the entire race. Alternating between running and walking is perfectly acceptable and may help prevent injury or excessive fatigue. Finishing comfortably is a worthwhile goal." Be sure to warm up on race morning With cooler weather arriving in Houston, Thanksgiving morning is expected to be one of the coldest of the year, according to reports. "Five to ten minutes of brisk walking or easy jogging, along with movements such as leg swings and marching, can help prepare your body for the effort ahead," Balle said. "Wear shoes and clothing you have already used during training. Race day is not the time to try something new." Eat a familiar breakfast Balle says runners shouldn't drink large amounts of water or overcomplicate fueling the morning of the race. " A familiar breakfast such as toast, oatmeal, or a banana one to three hours beforehand may work well, depending on your stomach and start time." Keep it in control and don't push through injuries "Once the race begins, it is easy to get swept up in the crowd and start too fast," Balle said. For the 5K: "Aim for a controlled first mile so you have something left for the finish." For the 10K: " Settle into a pace you can maintain for several miles before deciding whether to pick it up." "If your goal is simply to finish, use a pace that allows you to speak in short sentences," Balle said. "There is no rule that says you have to race every mile." item.description: The Daily Slop – 25 November Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Hail = Raised @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/VS4c8jPbmU — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 24, 2026 Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Defense vs Bengals This was a new Cover-0 look that I don’t recall seeing from Jones so far this season. Traditional Cover-0 is pure man-to-man coverage against all eligible receivers and no safety help in the middle, but this is almost like a three-deep zone variation of Cover-0. The Commanders put eight defenders on the line of scrimmage this time and all eight of them blitz. That leaves just three defenders in coverage as they effectively play the deep zones of Cover-3 behind the blitz. Burrow again looks to his top receiver in Ja’Marr Chase, but this time Chase is in the slot and spotting up as a hot route option. Burrow immediately pulls the trigger to avoid a sack and throws hot to Chase, but cornerback Rasul Douglas plays this perfectly. Douglas sits at the first down marker knowing the ball has to come out quick against the blitz. He knows Chase is Burrow’s go-to target and he spots Chase beginning to slow down and spot up underneath. So before Burrow even delivers the throw, Douglas begins breaking on the pass. This enables Douglas to arrive at Chase before the ball does and he goes over the top of him to nearly intercept the pass. The Commanders defense had an outstanding performance against the Bengals on Monday night. Daronte Jones stuck to his identity of aggressive blitzing and it paid off against one of the top offenses in the NFL. I broke it all down: https://t.co/Ro4PSrO3As pic.twitter.com/OuHITh0WH9 — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 25, 2026 Unfortunately, Douglas drops the interception on what would have been an outstanding play by him. It goes back to what I said on the previous play, the Commanders biggest issue defensively is finishing plays when they have the opportunity. Douglas dropped three interceptions in this game and this was one of them. It was still a terrific read and great play by Douglas, but it could have been so much better had he come up with the ball. The Green Bay Packers have a lengthy injury report heading into their Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , with eight players listed as questionable. The biggest storyline, however, is the anticipated return of Micah Parsons , who is expected to make his season debut Wednesday night. Parsons was officially activated from the physically unable to perform list, opening the door for his return after tearing his ACL and meniscus last December. While he remains listed as questionable, the All-Pro pass rusher is expected to play against the Rams, giving Green Bay’s defense a major boost for a matchup against Matthew Stafford. Parsons has been working his way back since returning to practice earlier this month. He has been limited throughout his ramp-up period, but Wednesday night could finally mark his return to the field. Green Bay will likely manage his workload as he gets back into game action, but having him available is an important development for a defense looking to make a statement against one of the NFC’s top teams. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Josh Jacobs is another major name to monitor. The Packers running back is questionable after remaining limited in practice with a finger injury. Jacobs has missed the last two games after undergoing surgery on his broken ring finger, but he returned to practice this week and has a chance to play against Los Angeles. Green Bay has six other players listed as questionable: linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive linemen Travis Glover and Sean Rhyan, guard Kevin Zeitler, and wide receivers Bo Melton and Skyy Moore. The offensive line is particularly concerning, with Rhyan, Zeitler, and Glover all dealing with injuries. Aaron Banks should play, despite being on the report. Green Bay needs as much protection as possible against a Rams defensive front of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, capable of putting pressure on Jordan Love. Getting those players active could prove important, especially if Jacobs is available and the Packers want to establish their running game. This is a massive game for both teams in the NFC playoff race. Green Bay and Los Angeles enter at 6-4, with the winner gaining the head-to-head tiebreaker in a race that could determine the final postseason spots. A loss would drop the Packers to 6-5, putting them in a tougher position with only seven games remaining. The Packers have a chance to get Parsons back at the perfect time, but their overall health could determine whether they can take advantage of the opportunity. item.title: Amy Hunt reacts to being named among Sports Personality of the Year favourites
item.description: British sprinter Amy Hunt says being listed among the frontrunners to win the upcoming BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award feels "very special". The 24-year-old enjoyed a successful summer at the European Championships, securing a clean sweep of four gold medals in the women’s 100m, 200m and relay before completing her tally in the mixed relay at Birmingham’s Alexander Stadium. The victories added to Hunt’s rapidly growing collection of honours, which already includes world and Olympic silver medals. Hailing from Newark, the sprinter has been highlighted as one of the favourites to receive the prestigious Sports Personality of the Year Award, which will be presented on December 13. Among the other contenders in the conversation are Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane , England midfielder Jude Bellingham , skeleton racer Matt Weston and middle-distance runner Josh Kerr . Amy Hunt won four golds at the Europeans (PA Wire) Speaking to the Press Association, Hunt said: "It’s so incredibly special because it’s such a point of national pride. I always grew up watching it with my parents. "It’s such an iconic event and it holds such a place in our hearts as British people. "We are such a sporting nation and we really believe that we can take on the best of the world from this tiny little island. "To be named alongside some of these very iconic figures of British sport with far more noise than I’m actually used to – it’s very special just to be part of the conversation. "It’s really special that track and field has been able to cut through to the cultural consciousness this year, it’s great to be spearheading them." Hunt competed at her debut Olympic Games at Paris 2024 , where she narrowly missed out on reaching the 100m final, but believes she will be far better equipped for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. The athlete, who also earned an English degree from Cambridge, revealed that she thinks about the event every day. She added: "I’ve already been training for it, it is constantly in our big picture. "Olympics generally are the underpinning core of what we do every single day. "LA is such an iconic place and when I think of the imagery of it and that hazy 80s, neon feel. item.title: Phillies lose third baseman Alec Bohm to free agency, signs with Royals
item.description: The Phillies have lost their most consistent right-hand hitting run producer to free agency. Often-maligned corner infielder Alec Bohm has agreed to a two-year, $20 million contract with the Kansas Royals, it was reported Wednesday morning. Over seven seasons, mostly spent as the Phillies third baseman, Bohm fashioned a .273 batting average. Despite only hitting .249 in 2026, Bohm finished second on the club with 88 runs batted in, posting one of the National League's higher marks for two-out hits with men in scoring position. Bohm added 15 home runs and 29 doubles in 155 games the past season. He had an on-base percentage of .315 and a .383 slugging percentage. Bohm was a minus-0.2 WAR last season, in part due to being considered an inconsistent defender as well as slow on the basepaths. The 30-year-old shifted to first base after the Phillies acquired Luis Arraez and rearranged their infield which moved Bryce Harper from first to right field. The third overall pick in the 2018 draft out of Wichita State, Bohm is fifth all-time for games played at third base for the Phillies. He was an All-Star selection in 2024, when he hit hit .280 and drove in 97 and smacked 44 doubles. He also had 97 RBIS in 2023, a campaign that featured a career-high 20 home runs. The club was rumored to have put Bohm on the trade block multiple times in recent seasons, but no specific offers were reported and he remained an everyday fixture at Citizens Bank Park. On April 11, 2022, in a home game against the New York Mets , Bohm was caught on TV saying, "I ----ing hate this place," after fans sarcastically cheered him for making a routine play following three throwing errors. He later apologized for his remark. The Phillies have prospect Aidan Miller as Bohm's potential replacement at third base. He was ESPN's No. 10 overall prospect heading into 2026, but missed almost the entire season with a back injury before returning for four games and then playing in the Arizona Fall League. Another option is Bryson Stott, who shifted to third from second base after the Arraez acquisition. item.title: Williams exceeded F1 cost cap by £627,000
item.description: Williams have had a difficult 2026 - uncompetitive and now in breach of spending rules [Getty Images] Williams broke Formula 1's cost cap during the 2025 season, governing body the FIA has found. The team say they "unintentionally" exceeded the cap by £627,000. Last season, the spending limit was $135m (£106m). Alpine were also found to have broken the rules, although theirs was a procedural breach without overspending. Both teams have reached so-called 'accepted breach agreements' with the FIA. Williams' involves a financial penalty, the amount of which has not been disclosed, and a 1.5% reduction in permitted aerodynamic research and development time for the next 12 months. Alpine have also been given an undisclosed financial penalty. Both teams must foot the costs of the investigations by the FIA into their rule-breaking. A Williams statement said: "The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. "We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap. "The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted co-operatively and in good faith throughout the review process. "Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future." The FIA said in a statement: "There is no accusation or evidence that (Williams) sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the cost-cap administration. "The financial regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by (Williams) in good faith. "Williams has accepted the FIA's interpretation and the resulting breaches." It said Williams' breach was the equivalent of a 0.48% overspend, which "falls at the lower end of the less than 5% minor overspend range". Williams' costs were incurred as the team tried to update their operations in order to become more competitive. Williams had targeted the new 2026 regulations as an opportunity to make a significant step forwards in the team's attempt to return to the front of F1. Instead, the team have taken a step backwards, and after finishing fifth in 2025, are lying ninth in the constructors' championship with two races remaining this season. item.description: The Snooker 900 Cup is being staged for a second year, after Neil Robertson won the first edition in 2025 [Getty Images] Ronnie O'Sullivan's poor form continued with a 5-3 loss to 61-year-old Tony Drago at the Snooker 900 Crucible Cup. O'Sullivan lost to the Maltese former professional at the tournament in Reading, which is played in the Snooker 900 format that features a shot clock and frames that can last no longer than 15 minutes. The 50-year-old had won his opening match, beating Barry Pinches 5-2 on Tuesday. He was previously undefeated in the format, which is played outside of the World Snooker tour, having won the John Virgo Trophy and the Global Championship earlier in the year. In a rare appearance in a UK ranking tournament last month, O'Sullivan lost in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open to Ka Wai Cheung, the world number 110. The seven-time world champion subsequently lost 4-0 to Shaun Murphy in the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester earlier this month. He last won a ranking event at the World Grand Prix in January 2024 and, while he should reach the 2027 World Championships, he is in danger of slipping out of the automatic qualifying places for the 2028 edition. World champion Wu Yize and reigning champion Neil Robertson were also both eliminated on Tuesday, losing to Joe Perry and Pankaj Advani by respective scores of 5-0 and 5-2. Drago is a former world top 10 player who made his only ranking tournament final at the 1997 International Open, losing to Stephen Hendry. item.description: Henry Patten (right) will pair up with Neal Skupski for the 2027 season [Getty Images] Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with his doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy. Heliovaara and Patten joined forces in 2024 and won Wimbledon together for the second time in July. In a post on his blog, the Finnish player detailed the disappointment, shock and anger he felt when Patten phoned him with the news. "I got a lot of stick for calling Harri to tell him," Patten told BBC Sport before Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany. "I was crumpled over the toilet after the match and Harri, as he often does, had left very quickly to catch a flight back to his family. "It was ruthless - it was a really difficult decision for me to make for two reasons. "The first one is we are year-end number ones and we have a great track record together. "Secondly, me and Harri grew really close during that time. I still consider Harri one of, if not my best friend. "He's invited to my wedding in the summer. It was probably the first time in my career that I have had to make a decision like that, and I didn't enjoy it." Patten's new partner will be compatriot Neal Skupski, who says he decided in the space of a "very stressful few hours" to end his pairing with American Christian Harrison. Patten and Skupski could play their first match as a regular pair against Kevin Krawietz and Tim Putz to decide Britain's quarter-final against Germany on Thursday. There is little doubt the dust is still settling on a bruising weekend. "It was a very uncomfortable few hours, but we did speak over the phone for a long time,” Patten continued. "Obviously I wasn't expecting him to be over the moon about it, and he absolutely has every right to be angry. "But in that discussion I said I feel like this decision is based on the tennis. item.description: London Broncos have played at The Cherry Red Records Stadium since 2022 [Getty Images] London Broncos will return to Super League in 2027 after being confirmed as the competition's 15th team. The club will return to the top flight for the first time since 2024 after being selected following a decision to expand the competition from 14 to 15 teams. The Broncos enjoyed a dominant 2026 campaign in the Championship, winning the League Leaders' Shield, Grand Final and 1895 Cup to complete a historic treble. Super League clubs voted in favour of expansion earlier this month, with the Rugby Football League (RFL) then tasked with identifying the additional team. London finished 16th in the 2026 IMG club gradings, below Championship rivals Barrow Raiders, who were initially considered for the available place. However, Barrow and the RFL recognised the Cumbrian club would not be ready to compete in Super League in 2027, leaving London as the next candidate. Super League chair Peter Hutton said: "We are delighted to welcome London Broncos back to Super League for 2027. "This is an exciting moment for the club and its supporters, and an opportunity to build a lasting presence for our competition in the capital." item.description: Senegal's football federation reacted to the Cas verdict on social media with a picture of the side lifting the Afcon trophy alongside the caption "again and always champions of Africa" [Getty Images] "Justice for sport." That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions. The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless. Following a hearing in Lausanne in October, a three-man Cas panel unanimously overturned that ruling by Caf, effectively judging that the decisions taken by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala in restarting the match and playing it to a conclusion were final. Morocco's football federation (FRMF), however, says it will "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". The North Africans could yet take their fight to the Swiss Federal Court. Those in Senegal have celebrated the return of the title, while several legal experts have backed the Cas verdict. Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling Teranga Lions pay tribute to fans Senegal's talisman Sadio Mane, who was named player of the tournament at Afcon 2025, said the ruling "fills us with joy". The 34-year-old former Liverpool man thanked his team-mates and Senegal staff as well as the whole Senegalese nation at home and abroad. "Your faith in us gave us strength during the most difficult moments. This victory is yours, too," he said in a statement on social media. Senegal captain Kalidou Koulibaly, who missed the final through injury, echoed that sentiment. "Some victories are won on the pitch, while others are won in the heart of a people," he said in a post on Facebook. "This one is both. "Long before this verdict, there was you - your prayers, your flags in the windows, your fervour, and the pride that unites us all: the pride of the people of Teranga." Pape Gueye, the man who scored the extra-time winner in Rabat, described the Cas decision as "an immense relief". Both he and Mane had a message of support for Morocco. "Senegal and Morocco are brotherly nations; may our shared passion for football continue to bring us closer together," Mane said. Gueye added: "Beyond football, the respect and fraternity between our two peoples remain what matters most. Let's hold on to that. "In the end, it is Africa that wins." item.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Brandel Chamblee believes that the time has come for the PGA Tour to get rid of all safety nets that enable players to remain at the highest level long after they have achieved any notable success. The 2027 season on the PGA Tour is going to be very interesting. Thoughts are already turning to the big changes which are coming in from 2028, with the tour set to be split into two tiers. The idea is for the narrative surrounding promotion and relegation to become much more prominent. However, players have had plenty of opportunities to put themselves in an extremely strong position heading into 2028. For example, Marco Penge nearly lost his full card on the PGA Tour at The RSM Classic. Not only did his victory at Sea Island move him into the top 100, it also ensured that he would be on the Championship Series in 2028. Meanwhile, both Aaron Rai and Ryan Fox will be exempt on the Championship Series until the end of 2031 after their major wins this season. Brandel Chamblee calls on the PGA Tour to get rid of safety nets for players There has also been some debate surrounding those who left for LIV Golf . For example, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm will presumably be exempt for the Championship Series in 2028 after serving one-year suspensions. Both men have won majors in the last three years. And speaking on The Big Swing with Jimmy Roberts about how the return of LIV players should be handled, Brandel Chamblee suggested that the PGA Tour needs to be much more ruthless. “I wouldn’t be surprised if some of these players have got to go back to the Korn Ferry Tour, got to go to the [Challenger Series], and then work their way into the Championship Series, and as they should. You’ve got to come back and prove yourself,” he said. “They’ve got a lot of safety nets on the PGA Tour. They should just do away with them. This would be very convenient for them to do away with these safety nets. If you really want to make golf more meritocratic, you need to get rid of these safety nets. Sports should always be answering the question: why are you here versus somebody else? And if the answer is because you did something great five or 10 years ago, that is the wrong answer. Watching undrafted rookie Drew Stevens line up his fifth kick of the night, I had total confidence he was going to split the uprights. As it turned out, my confidence was well-placed. Stevens drilled the game-winner to seal a 22-20 Week 11 victory, and the NFL officially recognized his primetime clinic by naming him the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week . K Drew Stevens has been named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after going 5-for-5 on field goals and 1-for-1 on extra point attempts in Monday Night's win over the Bengals. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
